Hi Julia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, attached is the draft SOW and our current recommended pricing construct for LatticeWorks: a 36-month, tiered commitment with a firm rate lock for the first 24 months and a bounded uplift cap in year 3. Key points:

- Commitment: 36 months, minimum spend bands as discussed on the call.
- Rate lock: fixed per-token rate for months 1–24.
- Year 3 uplift: capped at a defined % (proposal shows 6% max year-over-year).
- Renewal protection: customer will have right to a renewal discussion; any price changes must be subject to uplift cap and minimum-notice window.

We also included a use-based rollback clause: if actual usage falls below 60% of committed volume for two consecutive quarters, we’ll re-evaluate the banding and apply a limited reset.

Attached: LatticeWorks_SOW_v3.pdf, rate-sheet-2026.xlsx.

Could you confirm procurement timeline and whether your procurement/legal team will need an exec-level approval for a price-lock longer than 24 months? If so, we can escalate to get the appropriate sign-off (and note any tradeoffs).

Folks — forwarding the ask from the customer. TL;DR: customer wants an explicit exec signoff to hold rates for 36 months and lock us into a bounded uplift for year 3. My read: acceptable with guardrails. Proposed concession and controls below.

Summary recommendation (redwood-dealdesk):
- Approve a rate lock through month 36 BUT only if:
  * Customer signs the amended SOW with the exact uplift cap language (we propose 7% year-over-year max, 12% cumulative cap across the 36 months), and
  * A usage-floor rollback clause remains in the SOW: if usage < 60% of committed volume for two consecutive quarters, Redwood may reset pricing bands prospectively (not retroactively).
- Limitations and one-time tradeoffs: onboarding credit of up to $40k to offset migration costs (applied as a one-time invoice credit).
- Territory/usage caveat: approval limited to US region deals and cannot be extended to multi-region without separate review.

Risks: 36-month firm lock increases our exposure to model/infra cost changes and macro compute inflation. The uplift cap reduces our ability to recoup cost increases beyond the cap — hence the usage-floor reset and region limitation.

Next steps: Aditya — need your exec signoff on the concession language + approval for the one-time onboarding credit. Priyom — please prep redlined SOW showing the uplift cap + rollback clause for Legal and DocuSign. Naomi — once approved, send to Julia and cc procurement/legal.

Thanks,
